claims.claim: Epiphanius of Salamis was bishop of Salamis (Constantia), the metropolis of Cyprus.
Epiphanius was born c. 310–320 near Eleutheropolis in Palestine and died in 403 at sea on his return journey from Constantinople to Cyprus.
Epiphanius was consecrated as Bishop of Salamis in 367 and served as bishop for nearly forty years.

The Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts is a Byzantine Rite liturgical service performed on weekdays of Great Lent and the first three days of Holy Week, in which communion is received from Gifts sanctified in advance.
The Presanctified Liturgy has no anaphora (Eucharistic Prayer).
The full Divine Liturgy having a joyful character is not in keeping with the somberness of the season of repentance, so the Presanctified is substituted during Great Lent.
The Presanctified Liturgy is structured much like other vesperal divine liturgies prescribed for strict fast days.
The liturgical text attributed to Epiphanius includes prayers for catechumens and prayers of the faithful, with rubrics indicating actions by the priest and deacon.
The text contains a prayer for those preparing for holy illumination (baptism).
The liturgy includes a prayer said after the holy gifts have been placed aside, and a prayer behind the ambo.
